previous_disclosures.section: NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS > 30. CONTINGENCIES > Interchange Fee Litigation
previous_disclosures.summary: Citigroup and related entities are defendants in the IN RE PAYMENT CARD INTERCHANGE FEE AND MERCHANT DISCOUNT ANTITRUST LITIGATION, a multi-district proceeding in the Eastern District of New York. Plaintiffs, including merchants, allege violations of the Sherman Act and California statutes regarding conspiracy to set interchange fees and restrain trade, as well as anticompetitive aspects of Visa and MasterCard IPOs.

previous_disclosures.section: NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS > 30. CONTINGENCIES > Interchange Fee Litigation
previous_disclosures.summary: A 2014 class settlement was reversed in 2016, leading to a new 2019 settlement approved by the district court. comparisons.peer_topic: Variable Rate Demand Obligations Antitrust Litigation Status
comparisons.peer_summary: GS&Co. is a defendant in a consolidated putative class action alleging a conspiracy to manipulate the market for variable rate demand obligations (VRDOs) through federal antitrust and state law claims. While Group Inc. was dismissed in 2019 and various state law and fiduciary duty claims against GS&Co. were dismissed by the district court in 2020 and 2022, the federal antitrust claims remain active as the proceedings are stayed pending an interlocutory appeal of the 2023 class certification grant by the Second Circuit.
comparisons.comparison: Both C and GS are defendants in consolidated antitrust class actions involving financial market benchmarks/practices where the procedural status involves appeals and stays. C's interchange litigation involves a damages settlement affirmed by the Second Circuit in March 2023 and a separate injunctive claim, while GS's VRDO litigation involves federal antitrust claims that are stayed pending an interlocutory appeal of a class certification grant by the Second Circuit. Both disclosures highlight the role of the Second Circuit in managing the procedural trajectory of their respective antitrust matters.

sentences.text: On March 15, 2023, the United States Court of Appeals for the Second Circuit affirmed the district court's final approval of the damages class settlement and remanded the case back to the district court for administration of the settlement claims process.
The settlement involves the damages class only and does not settle the claims of the injunctive relief class or any actions brought on a non-class basis by individual merchants.

Group Inc. and GS&Co. were among the defendants named in a putative class action relating to variable rate demand obligations (VRDOs), filed beginning in February 2019 under separate complaints and consolidated in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York.

On June 28, 2022, the court granted in part and denied in part the defendants' motion to dismiss, dismissing the state breach of fiduciary duty claim against GS&Co., but declining to dismiss any portion of the federal antitrust law claims.

comparisons.peer_summary: The monetary relief class action settled for ~$6.2 billion with $700 million returned to defendants; a separate injunctive class action saw preliminary approval denied in June 2024, while individual actions by opting merchants have mostly settled representing over 70% of sales volume. Ongoing matters include a Swiss EURIBOR investigation and a U.S. Court of Appeals affirmation of a dismissal in an antitrust lawsuit; the Firm has resolved all non-U.S. dollar LIBOR actions and obtained dismissals or moved for summary judgment in remaining U.S. dollar LIBOR cases.
comparisons.comparison: Both C and JPM disclose status updates on the same consolidated antitrust litigation regarding payment card interchange fees, specifically noting that a damages class settlement was approved and an injunctive relief class settlement was denied preliminary approval in June 2024. JPM explicitly states that the monetary relief class action settled for ~$6.2 billion (consistent with C's $6.24 billion figure when accounting for returns/adjustments) and confirms the June 2024 denial of preliminary approval for the injunctive class action, mirroring C's disclosure of the same event. C notes the Second Circuit affirmed the damages settlement in March 2023, while JPM mentions the settlement was 'approved and administered' in prior years, but both highlight the June 2024 injunctive denial as a key 2024 development.

sentences.text: On March 15, 2023, the United States Court of Appeals for the Second Circuit affirmed the district court's final approval of the damages class settlement and remanded the case back to the district court for administration of the settlement claims process.
On June 25, 2024, the district court denied the motion for preliminary approval of the injunctive relief class settlement.
A separate class action seeking injunctive relief continues, and in September 2021, the District Court granted plaintiffs' motion for class certification in part, and denied the motion in part.

In June 2024, the District Court denied preliminary approval of a settlement of the injunctive class action in which Visa and Mastercard agreed to certain changes to their respective network rules and system-wide reductions in interchange rates for U.S.-based merchants.

comparisons.peer_topic: VRDO Antitrust Litigation Class Certification Appeal
comparisons.peer_summary: In City of Philadelphia v. Bank of America Corporation et al., the court denied state law claims but allowed U.S. antitrust claims to proceed, and granted class certification on September 21, 2023. The Second Circuit granted leave to appeal the class certification decision on February 5, 2024.
comparisons.comparison: Both C and MS face consolidated antitrust class actions where the courts have granted class certification, leading to active litigation or settlement processes. C's interchange litigation involves a certified damages class with a settlement affirmed by the Second Circuit, while MS's VRDO litigation involved a court granting class certification in September 2023, which is now under appeal to the Second Circuit. Both disclosures reflect the risk and procedural complexity associated with certified classes in antitrust litigation against banks.

sentences.text: On March 15, 2023, the United States Court of Appeals for the Second Circuit affirmed the district court's final approval of the damages class settlement and remanded the case back to the district court for administration of the settlement claims process.
This proceeding is captioned IN RE PAYMENT CARD INTERCHANGE FEE AND MERCHANT DISCOUNT ANTITRUST LITIGATION.

On November 2, 2020, the court granted in part and denied in part the defendants' motion to dismiss the consolidated complaint, dismissing state law claims, but denying dismissal of the U.S. antitrust claims.

Plaintiffs allege, inter alia, that the Firm, together with a number of other financial institution defendants, violated U.S. antitrust laws and relevant state laws in connection with alleged efforts to artificially inflate interest rates for Variable Rate Demand Obligations ("VRDO").
